analysis.title: Europe Healthcare: Sector check in: Monitoring sector valuation, earnings execution and innovation momentum
key_insights: 3Q26 earnings tracker for European BioPharma: 60% of companies beat revenue and 86% beat earnings, vs 64%/91% in 2Q26 and 40%/70% in 1Q26. GSK has met or beaten consensus revenue and earnings at every report since 1Q24.

Post-3Q26 consensus FY26 revisions are +2% on revenue and +3% on EPS across the group. Novo had the largest upgrades (+7% revenue, +12% EPS). Novartis had the largest negative EPS revision (-5%) despite +1% revenue and +4% operating profit revisions.
GSe forecasts sit 1% above consensus on sales and 2% above on core EBIT across 2026-2028 for EU Large Cap Pharma and BioPharma. The most upside risk vs Visible Alpha consensus is at UCB and Sanofi.

FX outlook for 2026 improved. Galderma, GSK, Novo, Roche and Sanofi revised FX guidance favourably. Roche, GSK, Sanofi and Novo guide to an average -1.5% revenue and -3% earnings FX impact for 2026, vs -2%/-3% revenue and -4% earnings at 2Q/1Q26.
Novartis, Galderma, AstraZeneca and Sandoz guidance implies FX tailwinds of 1-2% on revenue. Roche's 3% turnover drag implies a 5% hit to core operating profit and EPS.
Clinical execution has moderated. The sector Phase 3 success rate is 60% YTD in 2026, vs 82% at 1Q26, 75% at 2Q26 and 71% in FY25. The trailing 12-month delivery rate is 55%, down from 69% at 2Q26.

Argenx, AstraZeneca and Roche are above the sector-average YTD Phase 3 success rate among companies with more than one readout. Roche leads the trailing 12-month rate at 80% on five readouts. Novo (2 of 6) and Sanofi (1 of 3) are at 33%.

Of 19 new molecular entity Phase 3 readouts YTD, eight were positive, nine negative and two mixed. Roche had the strongest NME record (two of three positive). AstraZeneca produced the most NME data (three positive of six).

R&D success and share performance have diverged. AstraZeneca has a 55% 12-month Phase 3 delivery rate and the stock is -7% over 12 months (16.3x vs 17.6x P/E). Novartis has a 50% rate and the stock is +14% (17.7x vs 15.5x).
GS ranks AstraZeneca the innovation leader on absolute positive readouts and approvals, success rate on key readouts with over $500mn potential, and number of first/best-in-class assets.

Valuation: EU large cap pharma trades at 13.6x 12-month forward P/E, a 3% discount to SXXP. The discount was 13% in Aug and 10% in May 2026. The sector has averaged about a 1% premium over 25 years. US large cap pharma trades at 20.7x, about a 54% premium to EU, vs a 9% 10-year average premium.

GS stays cautious on the sector given the upcoming loss-of-exclusivity cliff, mixed clinical delivery and modest near-term earnings growth. Average annual LoE drag is about 2% over FY26-30. The impact rises in the 2030s, with Sanofi most affected.

Buy-rated: AstraZeneca (growth plus pipeline optionality), Bayer (underappreciated Pharma business, glyphosate settlement ruling expected before Christmas), Argenx (on Conviction List), Galderma and UCB (outsized revenue growth), Sandoz (biosimilar LoE opportunity). Novartis is Sell. GSK, Novo, Roche and Sanofi are Neutral.

Novartis Sell thesis: generic headwinds reset the growth rate. Shares rebounded about 20% since Sept 9 (SXDP +17%) and buyback pace rose from 130k to 400k shares a day. GS sees the outperformance as unjustified ahead of the LoE waves.

Roche: GS giredestrant 2027 sales estimate of CHF400m/$480m is below company consensus of CHF638m/$762m. GS sees headline risk from EMBER-4 (Lilly) and CAMBRIA-1 (AstraZeneca) readouts with Roche at 17.4x 2027E EPS, about a 20% premium to the sector.
Sanofi trades at 8.8x 2027E EPS, a 55% discount to the sector. Investors are waiting for clarity on strategy and organic vs M&A growth after the expanded Regeneron collaboration.

Novo: GS expects about 1% CER growth in 2027 and about 2% at operating profit, with mid single digit growth returning from 2028. Debates centre on the ex-US Wegovy pill launch and 2027 earnings growth.

AstraZeneca catalysts: AVANZAR readout delayed to 1Q27 (GS models 40% probability of success), oral PCSK9, Datroway readouts, CAMBRIA-1, saruparib and dapagliflozin combinations. GS supports the $80bn 2030 revenue target.

Argenx: the December Phase 3 empasiprubart readout in MMN is key to showing development capability beyond Vyvgart. GS sees risk from the small Phase 2 dataset and uncertainty on IVIg-comparable efficacy.

M&A capacity is about $600bn for large cap pharma at 3x EBITDA leverage. GSK leads EU coverage by deal value (c.$15.8bn), including Nuvalent at $10.6bn upfront. Novartis is most active by count with seven deals. Oncology (30%) and immunology (27%) lead deal focus, with growing China licensing and AI-integrated partnerships.
UCB: the guidance upgrade and the INTREPID lutikizumab topline remove one competitor overhang on Bimzelx. Remibrutinib RECHARGE readouts are the remaining watch item.

Sandoz: GS cites over $275bn of LoE value across 2026-36 supporting a double-digit biosimilar growth path. The 3Q26 update missed revenue by 2% and narrowed sales guidance to the bottom end while raising core EBITDA margin guidance.

market_movers.rationale: Best-in-class mix of growth and pipeline optionality with valuation seen as increasingly attractive. 3Q26 beats on revenue (2%), operating profit (9%) and EPS (8%).
Potential glyphosate settlement approval before Christmas and under-appreciated Pharma growth. 3Q26 EPS missed by 14% but guidance was raised.
On the European Conviction List. Outsized growth and pipeline optionality, with the December empasiprubart MMN Phase 3 readout as the key catalyst.
Galderma growth and margin expansion seen as best-in-class on the Nemluvio ramp and aesthetics momentum.
UCB Bimzelx growth intact on head-to-head superiority, guidance upgrade and competitor overhang removal. GSe shows the most upside vs consensus.
Sandoz is well placed for the biosimilar loss-of-exclusivity decade with over 100 biosimilars targeted by 2040.
Patent expirations and a structural growth reset are not reflected in a premium valuation. Recent outperformance seen as unjustified.
Limited pipeline optionality and modest Exdensur and Blenrep launches, with risk to the over £40bn 2031 revenue guidance.
Debate centres on the ex-US Wegovy pill launch and 2027 earnings growth. GSe expects about 1% CER growth in 2027.
Long-term upside is largely priced in at a premium multiple, with 2027 risk from the giredestrant launch and competitor adjuvant breast cancer readouts.
Strategic direction uncertainty keeps investors on the sidelines despite a 55% sector discount. Earnings upside depends on Dupixent.

sector_views.rationale: GS remains cautious at the sector level given the loss-of-exclusivity cliff, mixed clinical delivery and modest near-term earnings growth, despite a discount to history.
More than $275bn of loss-of-exclusivity value across 2026-36 supports double-digit market growth.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported: 60% of covered companies beat revenue consensus and 86% beat earnings consensus (reported, vs consensus), vs 64%/91% at 2Q26.
Argenx 3Q26: revenue beat by 7%, operating profit missed by 9% (19% beat excluding one-off SG&A), EPS beat by 3% vs consensus.
AstraZeneca 3Q26: revenue beat by 2%, operating profit by 9%, EPS by 8% vs consensus. Guidance reiterated.
Bayer 3Q26: revenue in line (1%), EBITDA pre-specials beat by 13%, EPS missed by 14% vs consensus. Guidance raised on sales and EBITDA pre-special items.
GSK 3Q26: revenue in line (1%), operating profit beat by 5%, EPS beat by 8% vs consensus. Guidance improved on both top and bottom line.
Novartis 3Q26: revenue in line, operating profit beat by 8%, EPS beat by 7% vs consensus. Core operating profit guidance raised, sales reiterated.
Novo Nordisk 3Q26: revenue beat by 8%, operating profit by 12%, EPS by 14% vs consensus. Guidance raised on sales and operating profit growth.
Sanofi 3Q26: revenue beat by 9%, operating profit by 26%, EPS by 26% vs consensus. Sales guidance raised and EPS guidance specified.
Sandoz 3Q26 sales update: revenue missed by 2% vs consensus. Sales narrowed to the bottom end of guidance, core EBITDA margin guidance raised.
Share price moves on results day: Argenx 0%, AstraZeneca 7%, Bayer 4%, Galderma 7%, GSK -5%, Novartis 1%, Novo 6%, Roche 0%, Sandoz -3%, Sanofi 5%.

risk_factors: Loss-of-exclusivity cliff weighing on sector earnings, with the impact increasing in the 2030s (Sanofi most affected).
Declining Phase 3 success rate across the sector, now 60% YTD and 55% on a trailing 12-month basis.
Argenx empasiprubart MMN Phase 3 readout in December carries risk from the small Phase 2 dataset.
AstraZeneca AVANZAR readout in 1Q27 is a multi-year overhang.
Roche exposure to EMBER-4 and CAMBRIA-1 readouts given a premium multiple.
Bayer glyphosate settlement court approval and Crop Science performance.
US Pharma tariffs and MFN pricing policy.

tension_points.bull_case: EU pharma trades at a 3% discount to the European market and below its history (about 1% 25-year average premium), with positive post-3Q26 revisions of +2% revenue and +3% EPS.
tension_points.bear_case: Fundamentals look challenged in aggregate given the LoE cliff, mixed clinical delivery (60% Phase 3 success YTD) and modest near-term earnings growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Shares are near all-time highs with a faster buyback and a lower-risk catalyst path ahead.
tension_points.bear_case: A step-up in generic headwinds resets growth and the premium valuation does not reflect LoE downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Ongoing positive earnings momentum, stronger-than-anticipated key franchise sales, or unexpected pipeline success.

tension_points.bull_case: Phase 2 ARDA data, trial design, statistical simulations and physician feedback support a positive outcome.
tension_points.bear_case: Small Phase 2 dataset and uncertainty on true IVIg efficacy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A negative Phase 3 EMPASSION readout in December.
